name: Face-Reconstructed Gauss Smoothing
definition: A second point-data field storing a face-reconstructed value obtained from the voxel value, six neighbor-averaged face values, and two-point Gauss quadrature inside each voxel.
summary: Face-Reconstructed Gauss Smoothing reduces discretization artifacts by reconstructing a quadratic polynomial from voxel centers and face averages, then sampling it at Gauss points to capture local gradients better than simple averaging.
